A1.question: How is the ratio R optimised: the objective the optimiser actually works on

A92.question: How is the maximum of f*f (the L-infinity norm) handled in the optimised objective

A4.question: Which local optimiser solves the inner problem

A5.question: How is the number of steps n chosen and changed

A93.question: What is the macro shape (the envelope) of f across its domain

A94.question: What is the fine structure of f (the comb of teeth or blocks)

A95.question: Once converged, how does the program try to leave the local optimum

A85.question: Which part of f*f does the program's step aim at

A1.v371.name: Dinkelbach: maximise ||f*f||_2^2 - lambda*||f*f||_1*smoothmax(f*f), then lambda = R, repeated
A1.v371.note: iterated Dinkelbach (fractional programming); behind every construction above 0.962 (EinsteinArena thread 133 (https://einsteinarena.com/problems/second-autocorrelation-inequality, discussions))

A1.v372.name: Gradient steps on R itself (or log R) with a smooth max
A1.v372.note: the direct route: vanishing gradients on the flat top (EinsteinArena thread 133 (https://einsteinarena.com/problems/second-autocorrelation-inequality, discussions))

A1.v373.name: Active-set minimax: the tied maxima of f*f as constraints with dual weights (LP, SLSQP, persistent dual)
A1.v373.note: KKT view of the plateau (EinsteinArena thread 43 (https://einsteinarena.com/problems/second-autocorrelation-inequality, discussions); https://github.com/justinkang221/second-autocorrelation-inequality experiments/12, gpu_pd_optimizer)

A1.v374.name: Exact line search on R per block or run of f (no gradient)
A1.v374.note: packet/run-coordinate ascent: +1.5e-5 at 100k, then exhausted (EinsteinArena thread 92 (https://einsteinarena.com/problems/second-autocorrelation-inequality, discussions))

A1.v375.name: Alternating projection: push f*f towards a two-level target, then project back to f >= 0
A1.v375.note: Gerchberg-Saxton/Fienup; no gain in 1,370 trials on the leaders (EinsteinArena thread 212 (https://einsteinarena.com/problems/second-autocorrelation-inequality, discussions))

A92.v1.name: Exact maximum (a subgradient at the arg max)
A92.v1.note: kinked: smooth methods stall at the vertex (EinsteinArena thread 255 (https://einsteinarena.com/problems/second-autocorrelation-inequality, discussions))

A92.v2.name: LogSumExp smooth max normalised by max(f*f), beta annealed upward (1e5 to 1e9 and beyond, up to 1e14)
A92.v2.note: the leaders' choice; the normalisation keeps high beta stable (EinsteinArena thread 133 (https://einsteinarena.com/problems/second-autocorrelation-inequality, discussions); https://github.com/justinkang221/second-autocorrelation-inequality/blob/main/experiments/12_hyra_campaign/NOTES.md)

A92.v3.name: A fixed mild smooth max (beta about 100-500 relative to the max)
A92.v3.note: Adam-friendly; too smooth to resolve the 1e-7 ties at the top (EinsteinArena thread 133 (https://einsteinarena.com/problems/second-autocorrelation-inequality, discussions), CHRONOS)

A92.v4.name: A softmax- or p-norm-weighted set of the top lags
A92.v4.note: a smooth relative of the active set

A4.v161.name: L-BFGS on the smooth surrogate, many iterations per Dinkelbach round
A4.v161.note: the leaders' inner solver, 3-5 rounds per beta (EinsteinArena thread 133 (https://einsteinarena.com/problems/second-autocorrelation-inequality, discussions))

A4.v162.name: L-BFGS with Anderson acceleration of the Dinkelbach iterates
A4.v162.note: used in the July 2026 polish of the record's basin (https://github.com/justinkang221/second-autocorrelation-inequality/blob/main/experiments/12_hyra_campaign/NOTES.md)

A4.v163.name: Adam with gradient noise and elitist respawn of the worst candidates
A4.v163.note: Jaech & Joseph 2025 (published 0.94136; their released function has 2,540 steps; https://github.com/ajaech/autocorrelation_inequality)

A4.v164.name: Simulated annealing or random search on f

A75.v13.name: f = w^2 exactly (a cell at zero stays at zero: the support is locked)
A75.v13.note: the leaders' choice; the optimiser can't revive a dead cell (https://github.com/justinkang221/second-autocorrelation-inequality)

A75.v14.name: Clip or project to f >= 0 after each step

A75.v15.name: An explicit support mask pruned on purpose (zero the smallest cells, re-optimise, repeat)
A75.v15.note: warm self-pruning: set the record on the first autocorrelation problem (https://github.com/jmsung/einstein, wiki techniques)

A5.v198.name: Exact k-fold repeat np.repeat(f, k) (R unchanged), then polish at the finer grid
A5.v198.note: score-preserving to 1e-16; polish freedom grows with cells per tooth (EinsteinArena thread 212 (https://einsteinarena.com/problems/second-autocorrelation-inequality, discussions); https://github.com/justinkang221/second-autocorrelation-inequality/blob/main/experiments/12_hyra_campaign/NOTES.md)

A5.v199.name: Zero-pad to the size cap (2,000,000) and polish there, letting structure grow into the padding
A5.v199.note: the single biggest lever of the July record: about 10x faster gains per cycle (https://github.com/justinkang221/second-autocorrelation-inequality/blob/main/experiments/12_hyra_campaign/NOTES.md)

A5.v200.name: Average-pool a finer construction down to n, then polish (a basin transplant)
A5.v200.note: JSAgent: 1.6M pooled to 100k gave 0.96221, above any native 100k (EinsteinArena thread 180 (https://einsteinarena.com/problems/second-autocorrelation-inequality, discussions))

A5.v201.name: Coarse to fine, upsampling by interpolation between stages
A5.v201.note: works from small n (Jaech & Joseph); interpolating a tuned construction destroys it (EinsteinArena thread 211 (https://einsteinarena.com/problems/second-autocorrelation-inequality, discussions))

A93.v1.name: One heavy comb block holding about 30% of the mass at one end, an empty gap beside it, a graded ramp of bumps
A93.v1.note: the blueprint of the best constructions, found independently twice (EinsteinArena thread 254 (https://einsteinarena.com/problems/second-autocorrelation-inequality, discussions))

A93.v2.name: A tall spike plus a comb of smaller peaks

A93.v3.name: A smooth arcsine-like density, 1/sqrt(1 - 4x^2) on [-1/2, 1/2]
A93.v3.note: Barnard & Steinerberger: its autoconvolution is flat in the limit (arXiv:1903.08731)

A93.v4.name: A parametric series sum_j a_j (1 - 4x^2)^(j - 1/2) (about 100 terms)

A93.v5.name: Regular sparse packets under a smooth raised-cosine envelope
A93.v5.note: from scratch, caps at 0.903 (EinsteinArena thread 103 (https://einsteinarena.com/problems/second-autocorrelation-inequality, discussions))

A94.v1.name: A fine, coherent periodic lattice of teeth (period about 0.3% of the domain)
A94.v1.note: Hyra's innovation: half the relative period and twice the coherence of the older family (EinsteinArena thread 254 (https://einsteinarena.com/problems/second-autocorrelation-inequality, discussions))

A94.v2.name: Contiguous blocks with irregular spacing found by optimisation (hundreds to thousands of blocks)
A94.v2.note: the older family: 783 blocks at 100k, 3,133 at 1.6M (EinsteinArena thread 133 (https://einsteinarena.com/problems/second-autocorrelation-inequality, discussions))

A94.v3.name: A coarser parent with each cell split into about 20 sub-cells under a phase kernel
A94.v3.note: NIGHTFALL: a 100k parent to 2M, 0.962274 (EinsteinArena thread 287 (https://einsteinarena.com/problems/second-autocorrelation-inequality, discussions))

A94.v4.name: Number-theoretic support (Sidon/B2 sets, difference sets, quadratic residues)
A94.v4.note: caps at about 0.903 from scratch (EinsteinArena thread 127 (https://einsteinarena.com/problems/second-autocorrelation-inequality, discussions))

A94.v5.name: Regular [small, big, small] triplets
A94.v5.note: the 50k constructions of March 2026 (EinsteinArena thread 59 (https://einsteinarena.com/problems/second-autocorrelation-inequality, discussions))

A95.v1.name: Small noise (about 1e-8 x max f), then a full re-polish, with momentum along the last improving step
A95.v1.note: velocity cycles: sustained gains for 100+ cycles in the record's basin (https://github.com/justinkang221/second-autocorrelation-inequality/blob/main/experiments/12_hyra_campaign/NOTES.md)

A95.v2.name: Perturb along the gradient of the transition loss (lags where f*f crosses between its levels), re-polish
A95.v2.note: aims at where 2/3 of the loss lives (https://github.com/justinkang221/second-autocorrelation-inequality/blob/main/experiments/12_hyra_campaign/NOTES.md)

A95.v3.name: Perturb only the lowest 1-5% Fourier modes of f, then re-polish
A95.v3.note: about 70% of such moves improved, against about 0% for pixel noise (EinsteinArena thread 180 (https://einsteinarena.com/problems/second-autocorrelation-inequality, discussions))

A95.v4.name: Structural surgery on blocks (shift, scale, split, merge, remove), then re-polish
A95.v4.note: useful early; on the leaders, 6,000 block shifts gained nothing (EinsteinArena thread 212 (https://einsteinarena.com/problems/second-autocorrelation-inequality, discussions))

A95.v5.name: Exact single-coordinate moves on the tied plateau (incremental update of f*f, no FFT)
A95.v5.note: harvests about 1e-10 per move at the vertex (EinsteinArena thread 255 (https://einsteinarena.com/problems/second-autocorrelation-inequality, discussions))

A85.v4.name: The level transitions of f*f (lags with f*f/max between 0.1 and 0.9)
A85.v4.note: about 2/3 of 1 - R lives there, in under 5% of the lags; crossings are 8-11 cells wide (https://github.com/justinkang221/second-autocorrelation-inequality/blob/main/experiments/12_hyra_campaign/NOTES.md)

A85.v5.name: Only the tied maxima (the active set of the L-infinity norm)
